AbstractText.Label: STATEMENT OF PROBLEM
AbstractText.content: Pertinent evidence regarding the mechanical integrity of mandibular anterior teeth restored with a post-and-core is limited.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: The purpose of this finite element analysis study was to compare the impact of the post type (glass fiber post-and-resin core or cast post-and-core) along with the ferrule effect on the stress fields generated in endodontically treated mandibular lateral incisors and canines.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Three-dimensional models of the segmented mandible were developed. Mandibular incisors and canines with or without a 2-mm circular ferrule and restored with a cast post-and-core or glass fiber post-and-resin core were simulated and subjected to linear elastic static analysis. The principal stress values were calculated. von Mises equivalent stresses were used to evaluate the stress.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Maximum principal stresses in dentin were highest in incisors, with a ferrule. Stress parameters in composite resin core in both incisors and canines were critically close to the tensile failure limit of the core material. Cast post-and-cores cemented in incisors without a ferrule accumulated the highest stresses, exceeding the tensile failure limit of resin-modified glass ionomer cement.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Tooth preparation with a ferrule led to a remarkable rise in stress in the dentin of mandibular incisors but favored the mechanical integrity of the restoration.
